summary: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) ecosystem has become the de facto standard for connecting AI agents to external tools, data sources, and services through a unified interface. By 2026, it spans three layers: aggregator platforms that bundle thousands of integrations, gateways/proxies that add auth and governance, and individual servers that expose specific capabilities like browser automation or repository access. This matters because MCP lets AI agents take real actions—querying databases, deploying code, controlling browsers—without bespoke integrations for each tool.
ecosystem_note: Aggregators (e.g., Composio, Smithery) bundle and route many MCP servers behind one managed platform, gateways (e.g., agentgateway, Cloudflare MCP) sit in front of servers to add authentication, security, and traffic control, while individual servers (e.g., Playwright MCP, GitHub MCP) each expose one specific service or capability.

tools.name: Playwright MCP
tools.connects_to: Browser automation—navigate pages, fill forms, click elements, check state, and run end-to-end web flows
strengths: Most-used MCP server in the community (ranked #1 globally in public usage)
Cross-browser automation support
Backed by Microsoft and the mature Playwright project
Ideal for agent-driven web flows and testing
tools.best_for: Agents that need to run real browser flows: navigate, fill forms, click, and verify state

tools.name: GitHub MCP Server
tools.connects_to: GitHub repositories, issues, pull requests, Actions, and code search via an OAuth-secured remote endpoint
tools.pricing_paid: Free (included with GitHub account; usage subject to GitHub plan)
strengths: Official, enterprise-backed by GitHub
OAuth-secured remote server—no local install, CI-friendly
Core to automated repo management and issue triage
Consistently a top pick across Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex
tools.best_for: Automating repository workflows, issue triage, and PR management

tools.name: Composio
tools.connects_to: 250+ apps and tools (GitHub, Slack, Playwright, databases) with a self-learning tool-selection layer
tools.pricing_paid: Usage-based and team/enterprise tiers (paid plans for higher volume and SSO)
strengths: 1B+ tool calls run on the platform
Self-learning layer improves tool selection and token efficiency over time
Repeat tasks run ~30% more accurately on 2x fewer tokens
Broad managed integration catalog
tools.best_for: Teams wanting managed, optimizing access to many tools from one platform

tools.name: Context7
tools.connects_to: Up-to-date, version-specific library documentation and code examples injected into agent context
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier; paid Upstash plans for higher limits
strengths: Top pick for coding agents in Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex
Eliminates outdated/hallucinated API usage
Lightweight and easy to add
Widely recommended default for developer workflows
tools.best_for: Giving coding agents accurate, current documentation for libraries and frameworks

tools.name: Figma MCP Server
tools.connects_to: Figma design files, components, and design-to-code context for agents
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier; paid via Figma plans for team features
strengths: Official OAuth-secured remote server
Bridges design files to code generation
Added to major aggregator catalogs in 2026
Strong adoption among front-end and design-engineering teams
tools.best_for: Design-to-code workflows and pulling design context into agents

tools.name: Filesystem MCP Server
tools.connects_to: Local files and directories with explicit scoped access via allowed paths or Roots
strengths: Default local file access server for many setups
Explicit access control—agents never wander outside granted paths
Reference implementation from Anthropic
Stays a default even as fancier alternatives appear
tools.best_for: Giving agents safe, scoped access to local files for coding tasks

tools.name: Smithery
tools.connects_to: Registry and hosting for thousands of MCP servers with one-click deploy and discovery
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier; paid hosting and team plans
strengths: Largest MCP server registry/discovery hub
One-click installation across clients
Hosted deployment of community servers
Central reference point for finding MCP servers
tools.best_for: Discovering, hosting, and deploying MCP servers from a central registry

tools.name: Cloudflare MCP
tools.connects_to: Remote MCP server hosting and gateway with OAuth, edge deployment, and Workers integration
strengths: Edge-hosted remote MCP with built-in OAuth
Eliminates local install and credential leakage risk
Scales globally via Cloudflare's network
Strong platform backing for production deployments
tools.best_for: Deploying secure, scalable remote MCP servers at the edge

tools.name: Chrome DevTools MCP
tools.connects_to: Chrome debugging—performance traces, network requests, console errors for diagnosis
strengths: Official Google server for browser diagnostics
Deep performance and network inspection
Added to major aggregator catalogs in September 2026
Complements Playwright for diagnosis vs. automation
tools.best_for: Diagnosing web performance, network, and console issues with agents

tools.name: Supabase MCP Server
tools.connects_to: Supabase Postgres databases, auth, storage, and edge functions via OAuth-secured remote endpoint
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier; paid Supabase Pro/Team plans
strengths: Official OAuth-secured remote server
Full database + backend access for agents
Popular among full-stack and AI app builders
No local install required
tools.best_for: Letting agents query and manage Postgres databases and backend services

tools.name: agentgateway
tools.connects_to: Proxy/governance layer in front of MCP servers—auth, security, routing, and observability for agent traffic
strengths: Purpose-built gateway for MCP and agent traffic
Centralizes authentication and access control
Observability and routing for multiple backend servers
Growing adoption for production governance
tools.best_for: Adding auth, security, and traffic governance in front of MCP servers

tools.name: Notion MCP Server
tools.connects_to: Notion pages, databases, and workspace content via OAuth-secured remote endpoint
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier; paid via Notion workspace plans
strengths: Official OAuth-secured remote server
Popular for knowledge and docs workflows
No local install, CI-friendly
Strong adoption in productivity and ops teams
tools.best_for: Letting agents read and update Notion docs, databases, and knowledge bases
